ring: Goku is calling! You can hear him chewing already.
Incoming call from Goku. He sounds out of breath, as usual.
Goku's ringing. Something about training, or lunch, or both.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Hey! It's me! Are you training? I'm training. Well, I'm eating, but I was training a second ago.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Can I ask you something? Do you like your habits?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Ha! That's honest. Which ones are the fun ones?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Hmm. That's the thing I don't get about people.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: When I was a kid, Master Roshi had me deliver milk every morning. I turned it into a race against the sunrise.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I never won, the sun's really fast. But I got super strong trying.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So I should turn mine into a game.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Yeah! If it's boring, add a rule. Beat your time, do it on one foot, do it before the kettle boils. Training's way better when you're grinning.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I met a guy today who was way stronger than me. It was awesome!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yeah! Isn't that great?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Nope! Got flattened. Best morning all week.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: If you only spar with people you can beat, you stay exactly as strong as you are.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Losing to someone better shows you everything you can't do yet. It's like a map.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: It still stings, though.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Sure it stings! Then you eat something, and you sleep, and you go back. And one day it doesn't sting, because you won.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Find something that's a bit too hard for you. That's where all the good stuff is.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Did you eat today? Like, properly? Not a sad little sandwich?

choice.text: I had a sad little sandwich.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Aw, no! That's not fuel, that's a snack pretending.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yes! See, that's how you get strong. You can't train on an empty tank.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: People think strength is all punching and running. Half of it happens at the table.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Chi-Chi always says I eat enough for ten people. But I train enough for ten people, so it's fair!

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I don't train like you.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Then eat like you, not like me. Just make it real food, and enough of it. Your body's trying to build something, give it the bricks.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Hey, you sound like you're thinking too hard. Your voice goes all squinty.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Planning's fine. Just don't plan so long you forget to do it.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Ah. Worrying's like running in place. Tiring, and you don't get anywhere.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: When I'm stuck, I just do the next thing I can do right now. Then the next. Usually the big problem goes away while I'm busy.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: And if it doesn't?

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Then at least you're warmed up for it! Ha!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Seriously, go move a bit. Your brain works better after your legs do.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I lost a lot when I was starting out. Like, a lot a lot.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Especially me! I was a kid with a stick and a tail, I didn't know anything.

choice.text: Did it make you want to quit?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Quit? Nah. It made me want to get back up faster.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: The thing is, every time I lost, I learned one thing. Then I didn't lose that way again.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: So losing is just how you collect the lessons. You can't skip it, it's part of the path.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I missed a few days this week. Does that count as losing?

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: It counts as one round! The match keeps going. Get up, shake it off, next round.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Do you ever train with friends?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: You should try it! It's way easier to show up when someone's waiting for you.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: That's great! Training alone is fine, but together is the best.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: When I trained with Krillin, we'd push each other every day. If he did fifty push-ups, I had to do fifty-one.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Then he'd do fifty-two. We got really strong really fast. And really hungry.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Friendly competition.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Exactly! Find someone to race. Or tell someone what you're doing. They'll ask you about it, and you won't want to say you skipped.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Okay, I'm calling to say something weird for me. Take a rest day.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Ha! I know, I know. But I mean it.

choice.text: I don't want to lose progress.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: You won't! That's the funny thing about rest.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: When I came back from training in heavy gravity once, I was so tired I slept for a whole day.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: And when I woke up I was stronger than when I went to sleep! The training goes in while you're resting.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So resting is training.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Resting is the second half of training! Just don't rest for a whole week. Then it's just napping.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I learned a new move today by watching a cat chase a moth. Did you know cats are really good at feints?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Sure! You can learn from anything if you watch closely.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: It's when you pretend to go one way and then go the other. Cats are sneaky about it.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Everything's a teacher if you're curious. The wind, a river, a really annoying fly.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: The day you think you know everything is the day you stop getting stronger.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So what should I learn today?

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Something small you didn't know this morning. Then tell me about it! I like new stuff.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Did I ever tell you about my grandpa Gohan? Not my son Gohan, my grandpa. My son's named after him.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yeah. He'd have liked my son. They're both really gentle.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: He found me in the woods when I was a baby and raised me in the mountains.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: He taught me to fight, to fish, to climb, and to say thank you for every meal.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Every morning we did the same exercises, even in the snow. I didn't know it was training. I thought it was just mornings.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: That's the best kind of habit.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Yeah! When something's just part of your day, you never have to argue with yourself about it.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I'm calling from my cloud! It's a bit windy, sorry!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yep! The Flying Nimbus! Master Roshi gave it to me when I was little.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Totally safe! Unless you fall off. Then it's a long way down.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: The cool thing about it is, only people with a pure heart can ride it. If you're not, you fall right through.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I always thought that was a fun rule. You can't fake being kind to a cloud.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Could I ride it?

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Hmm, maybe! Keep being good to people and doing your stuff. The cloud can tell.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Okay, I'll tell you a secret if you promise not to laugh.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Aw, come on. Fine, I'll tell you anyway.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I'm scared of needles. Like, at the doctor.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I've fought monsters the size of mountains and I'm fine. A tiny needle, and I'm out the window.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Everyone's scared of something.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Right? So if you're scared of something small, don't feel bad. Just do it anyway, like I do. Mostly. Chi-Chi has to drag me.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Guess how many bowls of rice I had for breakfast.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Ha! Three's a snack.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Close! I stopped counting at twenty-something.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: When Saiyans train hard, we get super hungry. Our bodies burn through everything.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: But I always eat slowly enough to taste it. Grandpa said food deserves attention.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: That's surprisingly wise.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Hey, I'm wise sometimes! Mostly about food. And fighting. Two topics. I'm very wise about two topics.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Bulma tried to teach me to drive once. It didn't go great.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: I kept forgetting the car can't fly. There was a fence. And a farmer.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: That's what I said! But apparently people find it weird when you fly to the shop.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I'm really bad at some normal stuff. Driving, forms, remembering birthdays.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: But I practise the stuff that matters to me every day, and that's what I'm good at.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: You can't be good at everything.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Nope! Pick your few things and do them every day. The rest, ask Bulma.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Did you know I had a tail when I was a kid?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Seriously! It was really useful for climbing trees.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Sometimes! It was great for holding snacks.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: The problem was, if anyone grabbed it, I got all weak and floppy. It was my big weak spot.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: So I trained it. Every day I squeezed it a little, until one day it didn't bother me anymore.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: You trained your weakness.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Yep! That's the trick. Don't hide the weak spot. Poke at it a little every day until it's not weak.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Bulma told me a fact and I can't stop thinking about it. Which is funny, because it's about thinking.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Your brain is only about two percent of your weight, but it uses around a fifth of your energy!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yeah! It's the hungriest part of you. Like me at a buffet.

choice.text: Is that why I'm tired after studying?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Probably! Thinking hard is real work.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: So if you skip meals and then try to do something clever, your brain's running on empty.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: So eating is studying.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Ha! I'm telling Gohan that. He'll say it's not scientific. But it kind of is!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I went fishing this morning and caught a catfish. Did you know they can taste with their skin?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Pretty much! They've got taste buds all over.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Ha! Imagine swimming through soup. Actually that sounds great.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: They live in muddy water where they can't see much, so they feel and taste their way around.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Isn't that cool? When one sense doesn't work, they got really good at another.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Like working with what you've got.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Exactly! If you can't train one way, train another way. There's always something you can do.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Okay, this one's my favourite fact ever, because it means sleeping counts as training.

choice.text: You just want to nap more.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: I always want to nap more! But listen.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: When you're in deep sleep, your body makes a bunch of growth hormone. That's when muscles repair and get stronger.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: So if you train hard and then skip sleep, you're doing all the work and skipping the part where you get paid.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: That's a good way to put it.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Bulma said it, I just remembered it. I remember facts about sleep and food really well. Funny, huh?

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I watched salmon jumping up a waterfall today. Like, straight up it! They're so strong!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: I caught two. But then I let one go, because it was trying so hard.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: They're swimming back to the stream where they were born. They find it partly by smell!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: They swim all the way out into the ocean, and years later they find their way back. Up waterfalls and everything.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: That's incredible.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Right? If a fish can find its way back after years, you can find your way back to a habit after a few days off.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Hey, have you had water today? Like, a real amount?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Some isn't enough! Have more.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yes! You sound stronger already.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Muscles are about three-quarters water. If you're dried out, they don't work as well.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Even a little bit thirsty and you get slower and grumpier. Ask Vegeta. Actually, he's always grumpy, bad example.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I'll go get a glass.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Get two! I'll wait. Actually, I won't, I'm going to lunch. Bye!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Do fish sleep? I asked Bulma and she said kind of!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: That's the funny part, most of them can't! No eyelids.

choice.text: How do you know if they're asleep?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: They just slow down and hover, all calm. Like they're meditating.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: So they rest with their eyes open, just floating there. Piccolo would love it.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Everything needs rest. Even fish, even in the middle of the ocean. Even me!

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Even you?

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Especially me! I sleep like a rock. Chi-Chi says I snore like an avalanche.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Hey! It's me! Are you busy? I'm not, I just finished lunch. Well, second lunch.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Hey! How many days in a row now?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: {streak}? Whoa! That's awesome!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: You know what that means? You're not trying to do habits anymore. You just do them. That's when it gets fun.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Right?! Now's a good time to add a bit more. Not a lot. Just a bit.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Don't be scared! Even if it breaks, all that training stays in you. The number's just the scoreboard.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: {streak} days! That's a great start!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: The first few days are like the first few punches in a fight. You're just warming up.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Slow's fine! Slow and every day beats fast and sometimes.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yeah! Go for it! Then go for two!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Zero days? That's okay! Zero means you get to start fresh. I love starting fresh.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Everybody does! Get back up. That's literally the whole thing.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yes! Let's go! Do one thing right now while we're on the phone. I'll wait.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Okay, I gotta go, I smell dinner. Keep training!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Hi! Bulma showed me how to read your chart thing. It's got lines and everything!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Bulma showed me your numbers. You did {week_checkoffs} habits this week!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: That's a ton! You're training like a Saiyan!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Don't thank me, you did it! But I'll take a little credit for cheering.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: If you feel good, it's not too much. If you're dragging, take a rest day. Your body tells you.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: That's solid! Real training, every week. That's how you get strong.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Then add one thing. Just one. Then see how it feels.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Totally! Steady is better than burning out.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Not many yet. Rough week?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: That's okay. Pick the easiest one and do just that tomorrow. Easy wins still count.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Ha, I forget stuff all the time! Put them somewhere you'll see them. Like next to the food. That's where I'd look.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Okay! Back to training. Or lunch. Both!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Hey, you're super good at {top_habit}! You've been doing it all the time!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: That's how you know it's yours now! It's like breathing.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Ha, me too! Well, I don't know what it is exactly, but I'm excited for you.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: When I got good at one technique, I used it to learn the next one. Everything builds on everything.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: So what's next? What would make {top_habit} even better?

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Nice! A bit longer each week. Don't jump too far.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Smart! Do the new thing right after. It rides along.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Keep going! I'm proud of you!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Hey! Okay, I'm supposed to tell you something. Hang on, I wrote it on my hand.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Bulma says you've been writing in that journal thing.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: {journal_streak} days in a row! I can't write that much. My hand gets tired before my brain does.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: That's cool. I think by punching stuff. Writing's probably quieter.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: She's the smartest person I know! If she says write, write.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Or, she says you should be. She asked me to remind you. So, reminder! Write something!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Just answer her question. Like you're telling a friend about your day. That's what I'd do.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Me neither! But you don't have to be good, you just have to do it. Like training.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Okay, I did my job. Now I'm going fishing!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Woah, I can feel your energy from here! What's your power level now?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: It's {power}.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Over a thousand?! That's awesome! When I started, I was barely past ten!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yep! Everybody starts small. You're doing great.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yes! Wait, no, Chi-Chi said no sparring in the house. Next time!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Hey, that's going up! Every day it goes up a bit. That's how it works for everyone.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Slow means it's real. Fast is usually a trick.

choice.text: I want to be as strong as you.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Ha! Then you'd better start eating more. And training. Mostly eating.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Keep it up! Bye!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Vegeta challenged me to a race this morning. Then he said I cheated. I didn't cheat! I just ran faster!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yep! Then he challenged me to another one. He's so fun.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: He's always a bit mad. It's kind of his thing.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: He acts like he hates me, but he's the best rival anyone could ask for. Every time I get stronger, he gets stronger too.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: And every time he gets stronger, I want to train even harder. It's like a ladder we keep building.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: You two need each other.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Don't tell him that! He'd explode. Like, actually. He's done it before.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I went to visit Master Roshi! He was asleep in his deck chair, but he says he was meditating.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: He was snoring, so... probably not.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yeah, he's super old! Like, really super old.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: He was my first real teacher. He made me deliver milk, plough fields and swim with sharks, all while wearing a heavy shell.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: I thought it was just chores. But it built everything. All my strength started in those boring mornings.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Small habits.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Yep! Don't tell him I said he was right. He gets really smug.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Piccolo used to be my enemy, did you know that? Now he's like family!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Time, I think. And he started teaching Gohan. He loves that kid.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: People can change a lot! Don't let anyone tell you they can't.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: He still doesn't smile much. But when Gohan does something good, his ears twitch. It's how you can tell he's happy.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: He's the best at staying calm. When I get too excited, I go sit with him for a while.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Everyone needs someone like that.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Yeah! Piccolo for calm, Bulma for brains, Roshi for wisdom, Vegeta for... yelling. And me for fun!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Bulma was the first person I ever met who wasn't my grandpa! She hit me with her car.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yeah, but I thought the car was a monster, so I threw it. We were even.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Ha, she says that too!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Then we went on a big adventure looking for the Dragon Balls. She made a radar to find them. I'd never seen a machine before!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: She's still my oldest friend. She's bossy, but she's always right. Okay, mostly right.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: Don't let her hear 'mostly'.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Ha! Good call. You're smart. Like her!

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Everyone came over for a big sparring day! It was the best!

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Nobody! Bulma made us stop because we broke her lawn.

then.speaker: GOKU
then.text: Yep! Even Master Roshi, though he mostly watched and ate snacks.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: Vegeta fought me, Piccolo fought Gohan, and Bulma shouted at all of us about the garden.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: You should come next time! You're getting strong enough.

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: I'd get flattened.

lines.speaker: GOKU
lines.text: That's the best part! You'd learn so much. Okay, maybe start with Krillin.
